transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-20 16:00 UTC | 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO), Sara (Head of ML), Raj (Eng Mgr), Ana (Security)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Diego our SE will run the demo.
00:14 - Liam: Hi, Liam here, CTO at Novus. We're looking at structured output for our fraud classification and a couple internal tools.
00:20 - Sara: Sara, head of ML. We'll own the model validation and evals.
00:26 - Raj: Raj, eng manager, I'll be coordinating infra.
00:30 - Ana: Ana from security. I'll focus on compliance and data flow.
00:36 - Diego: Awesome, quick agenda: show JSON mode with schema enforcement, function calling for downstream services, Console guardrails and Optimize recommendations; then Q&A and next steps.
01:05 - Diego: So quick context — JSON mode lets you declare a schema and Redwood will validate and either strictly enforce or coerce outputs; we also have function-calling where model outputs trigger calls to your microservices, and Console shows telemetry and template guardrails.
01:40 - Sara: When you say enforce, do you actually reject responses that don't match schema or do you attempt to coerce? We have strict types for risk tags.
01:50 - Diego: Good question. There are two modes: strict (reject + return structured error) or soft (coerce where possible and emit warnings). You can choose per-route. In demo we'll show strict mode returning an error payload — that helps downstream services avoid bad data.
02:20 - Maya: Also coverage in the Console, you can see schema match rate per prompt set, and Optimize will suggest quantization or batching profiles if cost/latency is off.
02:40 - Raj: On deployment — we're considering dedicated GPUs vs hosted. For PII-sensitive flows we might want VPC/private. How different is integration?
02:52 - Diego: Integration surface is identical: same API and SDKs. Private gives you customer-managed network and optional on-prem. Dedicated is reserved capacity; hosted is fastest to stand up. For VPC we support SAML and KMS integrations.
03:20 - Ana: SOC2, audit logs — do you keep token-level logs? We need audit trails for decisions.
03:30 - Maya: We have optional token-level cost/latency breakdowns and audit logs; for Private deployments logs can be customer-hosted. We can share SOC2 and ISO artifacts — I'll attach them after.
03:50 - Diego: Jumping into demo — I'm switching to Console. (typing) Here is a sample route configured for "fraud_classifier_v1" with a JSON schema: {\"transaction_id\": \"string\", \"score\": \"number\", \"flags\": [\"string\"]}.
04:15 - Diego: I'll run a prompt against the hosted model, JSON-mode strict. Watch the response — since the model sometimes returns natural language, Redwood's validator either returns the structured body or a validation error.
04:45 - Diego: Running... response... we got success, score 0.78, flags [\"high_amount\"]. Console shows schema match green, latency 320ms, token cost breakdown at the top.
05:10 - Sara: Nice, what about complex nested schemas? Our expected output has nested objects for payment metadata.
05:18 - Diego: We support nested schemas and arrays; we show the match rate per field in the Console. If nested mismatch occurs, the error payload includes a path to the failing element.
05:40 - Liam: How do you handle hallucinated fields that look valid but are made up IDs?
05:48 - Diego: Two levers: guardrails with allow-listing and function-calling to validate against your system. Example — we can wire a validation function that receives transaction_id and queries your service; the model calls the function when it wants to lookup.
06:10 - Diego: Let me flip to function-calling example. I'll demo a toy "lookup_customer" function. Model returns a structured payload that triggers the function call to our integration layer; Console shows the function call trace and result.
06:40 - Diego: Running... model returned payload referencing transaction_id T-9934, it called lookup_customer, we got 200 with customer status active. The final structured output now includes customer_verified true.
07:05 - Sara: That traceability is useful. Can function calls be gated so only verified functions run?
07:12 - Diego: Yes, we have RBAC on which functions are available per-route, and you can restrict to certain keys. Plus you can configure pre-call checks in the Console.
07:35 - Raj: From infra perspective, what's the network flow if we do private deployment? Do function calls leave the VPC?
07:45 - Diego: If private/VPC, function endpoints can be inside your network. For hosted, calls route through Redwood's integration layer — we offer private link options for dedicated customers.
08:10 - Ana: For compliance we need encryption at rest + KMS control.
08:18 - Maya: KMS/HSM integration is available for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can integrate with customer KMS via AWS KMS in supported regions.
08:40 - Diego: Back to schema guardrails — you can add human-readable validation rules in Console, e.g., "score must be between 0 and 1" and the runtime will enforce. We also surface failing prompts to a queue for review.
09:05 - Sara: What's your approach to prompts that produce slightly off values (0.9999 vs 1)? We have thresholds.
09:12 - Diego: You can define tolerances per-field in the schema or post-validate via function call. Console shows distribution of numeric fields so Optimize can suggest model variant or quantization.
09:40 - Maya: Quick note on Optimize: it analyzes your prompt set and suggests batching sizes and quantization levels to meet latency SLOs while lowering cost. For example it may recommend int8 conversion and batch size 8 for your 256-token average.
10:05 - Liam: Do you support deterministic outputs for audit traces?
10:12 - Diego: Determinism is tricky with modern models; options include low temperature + log-prob constraints, or we offer cached KV prefixing and reranking to increase reproducibility. All of these are configurable per-route.
10:40 - Diego: Now I'll demonstrate a malformed response scenario. I force a prompt known to confuse schema, and we get a validation error; Console shows the failing sample with attached diff and suggested guardrail (coerce field type).
11:10 - Maya: That diff is great for prompt engineering loops. You can tag prompts and auto-run evals.
11:25 - Raj: On throughput — if we run at 100rps, what does Dedicated look like vs hosted?
11:33 - Diego: Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools; hosted might have variability but faster onboarding. We can run pilot benchmarks: typical numbers for decoder LLM at 1k tokens on Ampere-class with batching are Xms/req (example numbers shown in Console). We'll run your workload and show real token/ms numbers.
12:05 - Sara: We want to instrument quality regressions. Does Redwood tie evals to rollouts?
12:12 - Diego: Yes — rollouts can be gated on eval metrics. If a canary shows drop in schema match or accuracy on your test prompts, we can auto-roll back. Console stores eval histories and issues regression alerts.
12:40 - Liam: On pricing — we need per-token and per-embedding numbers plus reserved capacity cost.
12:48 - Maya: I'll send a tailored pricing sheet. For pilots we often offer 2 weeks of dedicated trial capacity at a discounted rate.
13:05 - Ana: We'll need a security package and SSP.
13:10 - Maya: I'll attach SOC2, encryption, and network architecture docs. Also we can set up an NDA access for sensitive artifacts.
13:30 - Diego: Quick demo of function-to-toolchain: model calls a "create_ticket" function which posts to your Jira; we show the webhook and the function call audit. Console attaches full call payload and response.
13:55 - Sara: How do you prevent accidental PII exfiltration during those calls?
14:02 - Diego: We have data filters and redaction rules at the route-level and in integration middleware. Plus you can configure strip_fields before sending to external endpoints.
14:30 - Raj: For the pilot benchmark, what's needed from our side?
14:36 - Diego: A representative prompt set (approx 1k samples ideally), expected schema, and target SLOs (latency/cost). We'll run a 72-hour stress/baseline run and share dashboards.
15:00 - Sara: We can provide 800 sample prompts and a subset of edge cases.
15:08 - Diego: Perfect. We'll also provide curl examples and SDK snippets for JSON mode and function wiring.
15:30 - Maya: Any other questions?
15:34 - Ana: On data residency — can we keep logs in EU region only?
15:40 - Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported for hosted, and Private deployments can be fully localized.
15:58 - Liam: Ok, sounds promising. Next steps?
16:04 - Maya: Recap: Redwood to send pricing + SOW, security docs, and benchmark plan. Novus to send schema, prompt set, and schedule pilot kickoff.
16:20 - Raj: We'll get infra folks looped in.
16:30 - Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the deck and attachments.
16:42 - Liam: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
